To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
diabetes mellitus (DM) is a risk factor for endothelial dysfunction (ED) in micro- and macrovasculature.
the endothelium-dependent dilation in the microcirculation of the skin and in the macrocirculation of the forearm is reduced in patients with type 1 or 2 diabetes.
the endothelium-dependent vasoreactivity of the microcirculation and macrocirculation is significantly impaired in both type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of endothelial dysfunction in the development of diabetic complications.
the investigation of the pathogenesis of diabetic micro- and macroangiopathy.
the study of endothelial function, the role of the endothelial dysfunction in development of diabetic complications and the influence of different factors on the endothelial function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diabetes mellitus is associated with a higher risk for cardiovascular disease.
diabetes mellitus is a risk factor for endothelial dysfunction, and that the degree of dysfunction is correlated to the degree of hyperglycaemia.
the endothelium plays a crucial role in the pathogenesis of diabetes mellitus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endothelium plays a key role in the pathophysiology of diabetic micro- and macro-vascular complications, as well as in the development of the diabetic state itself.
the endothelial function of the micro- and macrovasculature is impaired in patients with diabetes, which is associated with the severity of diabetes.
we have shown that the endothelium plays a key role in the development of cardiovascular disease in diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endothelium is a key regulator of vascular tone and blood pressure, and that the endothelum is a key player in vascular disease.
the endothelial function of both micro- and macrovascular circulation is deteriorated in diabetic patients.
the endothelium, which lines the blood vessels, can sense the presence of pathogens and trigger the production of antimicrobial peptides.
